formula: will have + participle (completed before a future point) · will be + -ing (in progress at a future point) · by + time · this time next year
formula_visual: [By Friday] [I'll have finished] // [At nine] [I'll be working]
when_to_use: Future perfect for something COMPLETED before a future deadline — almost always with 'by' ('by Friday', 'by the time you arrive'). Future continuous for something IN PROGRESS at a future moment ('at nine tomorrow', 'this time next week').
when_to_use_ar: المستقبل التام لشيء مكتمل قبل موعد مستقبلي، وغالبًا مع 'by'. والمستقبل المستمر لشيء مستمر في لحظة مستقبلية.
why_arabic_speakers_struggle: Arabic rarely marks these distinctions explicitly, so learners use the simple future for everything. The forms also compress heavily in speech ('I'll have' → /aɪləv/), so learners who have only read them don't recognise them when heard.

examples.en: By Friday I'll have finished the report.
At nine tomorrow I'll be working.
This time next week we'll be flying to Turkey.
examples.ar: هذا الوقت الأسبوع القادم سنكون مسافرين لتركيا

examples.en: By the time you arrive, we'll have eaten.
By next year she'll have graduated.

common_errors.wrong: By Friday I will finish the report.
common_errors.correct: By Friday I'll have finished the report.
common_errors.explanation: 'by + deadline' needs the future perfect for completion.

common_errors.wrong: By the time you will arrive, we'll have eaten.
common_errors.correct: By the time you arrive, we'll have eaten.
common_errors.explanation: After 'by the time' use the present simple, never 'will'.

common_errors.correct: At nine tomorrow I'll be working.
common_errors.explanation: In progress at a specific future moment → future continuous.

practice_fill_blank.sentence: By the time you ___ (arrive), we'll have eaten.
This time next week we ___ (fly) to Turkey.

quick_rule: Completed by a deadline → will have + participle (use 'by'). In progress at a moment → will be + -ing (use 'at/this time').
quick_rule_ar: مكتمل بحلول موعد → will have + التصريف الثالث (مع by). مستمر في لحظة → will be + -ing (مع at/this time).
mnemonic: 'by' → will have DONE. 'at' → will be DOING.
connect_to_speaking: In accent week 4 you drilled /ləv/ for 'll have and /lbi/ for 'll be. Say 'By FRIday /aɪləv/ FINished' against 'At NINE /aɪlbi/ WORKing' — one sound sets the whole meaning.
